name: chown
summary: Changes the owner and group of files.
description: Gives files a new owner and/or a new group. The OWNER:GROUP form changes both at once; :GROUP changes only the group. Changing the owner usually requires root privileges (sudo).

options.description: Applies the change to directories and everything in them.
Prints a message for each file processed.

example.output: changed ownership of 'report.pdf' from root to esprit

options.description: Prints only the files actually changed.

example.output: changed ownership of 'project/build.log' from root to esprit

options.description: Changes the symbolic link itself rather than its target.
Copies the owner and group of another file.

arguments.name: OWNER:GROUP
arguments.description: New user, optionally followed by “:” and the new group.

examples.explanation: esprit becomes the owner of file.txt.
Changes the owner and group of the directory.
Gives the whole site to the web server, recursively.

dangerNote: Used with -R on the wrong path (for example /), chown can make the system unusable.
